source_caption:
🎬 A Patch of Blue (1965)

A Patch of Blue follows Selina D’Arcey, a young blind woman living an isolated and difficult life with her abusive mother and grandfather. Her world begins to change when she meets Gordon Ralfe, a kindhearted man who offers her friendship, encouragement, and a chance to experience life beyond the limitations imposed on her. As Gordon helps Selina develop confidence and independence, their growing connection challenges the racial prejudice and social expectations of 1960s America. Starring Sidney Poitier and Elizabeth Hartman, the film delivers an emotional story about compassion, courage, friendship, and the power of seeing beyond appearances.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Romance

⭐ IMDb: 8.0/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 45m • Not Rated

🎥 Director: Guy Green

✍️ Writer: Guy Green

🏆 Awards: Shelley Winters won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

source_details.title: A Patch of Blue
source_details.synopsis: A Patch of Blue is a 1965 American drama film directed and written by Guy Green about the friendship between an educated black man (played by Sidney Poitier) and an illiterate, blind, white 18-year-old girl (played by Elizabeth Hartman in her film debut), and the problems that plague their friendship in a racially divided America. Made in 1965 against the backdrop of the growing civil rights movement, the film explores racism while playing on the idea that "love is blind." Shelley Winters won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, her second win for the award, following her victory in 1959 for The Diary of Anne Frank. It was the final screen appearance for veteran actor Wallace Ford.
